Capacity (MW).note: The draft permit gives the MTU generators as 3,250 kilowatts each, so 83 engines make 269.75 MW. The 21 Cummins engines are rated 3,391 horsepower, about 2.53 MW each or 53.1 MW. The one Caterpillar engine is about 1.11 MW. The sum is about 324 MW. This is my own sum of the permit's ratings, and the permit states no total.

qa.question: Should capacity be 324 MW, summed from the newest draft permit?
qa.finding: The database shows 283.1 MW from the earlier fleet of 102 engines. The September 2026 draft permit (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Ae6Ctfv7oSCmhMZ%C3%89kDp%C3%89JKeyyrF%C3%897NeqHWN6Fd0wYTdl604KTTG6bsIhnFC9Sgq7vhd656jR%C3%895uQBkEpWYOBnMg%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true) lists 105 engines, with the MTU units now at 3,250 kW each. My sum of the permit ratings is about 324 MW.
qa.recommendation: Change Capacity to 324.0 once the permit is final, or now if you accept a sum of the draft's ratings. The earlier figure used 3.49 MW per MTU engine, which is the engine rating, not the generator rating.
qa.note: I read the Southwest Power Pool open queue list on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV). Entry GEN-2025-SR9 is 400 MW with no fuel shown, owned by OG&E, at the Muskogee 345 kV substation, with commercial operation in December 2029. Entry GEN-2024-293 is 248 MW of gas at the same substation name, with commercial operation in May 2033. Both are grid interconnection requests with no site address, and neither names this data center. They are added as separate projects, not as this plant's backup fleet. The permit has not been issued yet, so numbers could still change.
